utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at my request --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, before we start, I'd like to first briefly state what happened yesterday. At the end of our hearing, the electricity supply was, although not completely, but partly interrupted which caused most of the systems not to function anymore. The last words that were recorded in our system was an answer of the witness where he said: "Now, whether it coincides or whether it was planned to be that way, the date coincides with the date of the meeting in Oslo between," and there it stops. What then happened is recorded by the court transcriber but has not yet been uploaded in the system. The witness finished his answer. I don't know whether this was the last question, but then I instructed the witness, who understands some English, both about his duty not to discuss with anyone his testimony and I adjourned. That will then soon appear now in the system again. That's what happened yesterday. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would like to raise --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- the transcript I have, in fact, takes us to the very end, including Your Honour's directions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It could be that it is meanwhile there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I had risen to my feet yesterday as we were about to adjourn, just to raise the question of timing, to which I now return, in relation to this witness. I simply wanted to raise the issue of how long the examination of this witness is likely to take and the implications that that may have for the remainder of the week at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As the Chamber expressed earlier, the Chamber would like to finish with the two witnesses that are still scheduled for this week. Mr. Kearney, I don't know whether you could tell us how much time you would need for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, as you know, the next witness originally was a 92 bis witness. Our case in chief with that witness now will be extremely short. We anticipate about 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fifteen minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And it will be our strong -- our strong preference to finish him this week as well. We have -- this witness is already in The Hague, and we have a witness starting -- that we hope to start at the beginning of next week who has travelled some great distance. We believe we cannot move him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So, for the next witness, it would be relatively short. Could the Defence give an indication as to how much time it would need for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Also relatively short, I would have thought of something in the region of 30 to 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I think probably nothing from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I had indicated 15 to 20 minutes predicated on the examination before mine, but it could be shorter than that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time will the battle on the 92 ter statement take?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can't answer that question at the moment, but it certainly shouldn't take any court time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Hopefully, we will be able to expedite it once we agree about the reasons that the witness has been called, because there's a fair amount of information that's in the 92 ter statement. The dehors of the stated reason for this witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then that means that, for the next witness, we would not need the whole of the day tomorrow. We also know that estimates sometimes turn out to be real estimates but not always; so, therefore, in view of what I heard, I would say one session at least, if not one and a half, tomorrow should be reserved for the next witness. Of course, I have read the 92 ter statement which was distributed already. I see a few problems that could take some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think Your Honour has already given some indications in respect of that witness's 92 ter statement as to those passages which should be removed and those passages which can't be adduced without supporting material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then this would mean, Mr. Emmerson, that if we keep on the safe side that assuming that some time will be taken for re-examination tomorrow, that if you would try to finish cross-examination today, then we would --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I simply indicate, I've had an opportunity to discuss this issue with my colleagues. I don't think that Mr. Guy-Smith will have any questions or certainly many questions for this witness. I understand that Mr. Harvey is likely to have some. My concern - and Your Honour will have seen the breadth of the 92 ter statement - is that the use of 92 ter with this witness has meant that the Prosecution's been in the position to elicit his evidence in chief within a relatively short time, but there are really quite a large number of issues that I need to traverse with him in cross-examination. And it would be -- again, obviously, I will always, as I always do, abide by the Trial Chamber's rulings in respect of timing, but I had indicated at the outset that this was one of the witnesses whose cross-examination was likely to take some time. And, potentially, his evidence has implications which cut across quite a large range of issues, both generic and specific in relation to particular identified individuals on the indictment. And I would want the opportunity, if possible, in this particular instance to pursue those matters with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time do you assess you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, having sliced off as much of the fat overnight as I was able to over night, I was anticipating the first session tomorrow being the concluding session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would try to take one hour of tomorrow's first session, and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Well, we have the witness not in yet. Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, regarding the 92 ter statement for this witness, I just wanted to inform the Trial Chambers that the Court's redactions have been inputted into those. The new redacted document is in the process of being uploaded in e-court and should be ready this morning for both the parties and Chambers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that information. Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom. The curtains should be down when the witness enters the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Whilst that's being done, may I simply indicate, in respect of Mr. Kearney's last comment, that it may be that further redactions will be required, both in the light of evidence that was elicited yesterday and in the light of evidence that was not, because the indications that had been given yesterday morning incorporated in rulings left the Prosecution to explore the foundation of certain passages which Mr. Kearney chose not to explore in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it may be in respect of those passages --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it you'll first discuss it briefly --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- with Mr. Kearney, and then see what remains --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see what you are saying. The existing redacted draft may not be the final one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kearney, I take it you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm happy to talk with counsel outside of court today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was my understanding that the witness was nearby, but it turns out that he still has to climb a few stairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness 17.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have overcome the electricity-supply problems. I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony yesterday. Mr. Emmerson will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 17, yesterday, Mr. Kearney asked you some questions about the incident on the 4th of July when four FARK officers, who were en route to collect weapons, became involved in a confrontation in Gllogjan. And he asked you some questions about the effects of that incident on FARK soldiers generally. You remember those questions from yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, in your 92 ter witness statement, you refer to a meeting that took place the following day, at which that incident, amongst a number of other issues, was discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just ask my colleague to reference a specific paragraph number when he's referring to the statement, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I want to just remind you in respect of that meeting, in your 92 ter witness statement at paragraph 33, you indicate that at that meeting Tahir Zemaj said that he wanted the incident that had occurred the day before to be the first and the last of such incidents or he would be unable to forget. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that correct, Witness 17?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And you said that Mr. Haradinaj said at that meeting that it would not be repeated, nothing like that would happen again; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said that he was sorry about what happened and that would not be repeated.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Pause there. You can leave the statement to one side, Witness 17, and simply refer to it if I ask you to look at a particular passage. If you can, as best you can, answer the questions from your recollection. If we need to turn to the documents, we will. Now, we've seen various records that were made about that incident. I just want to ask you, please, to confirm that between the time of your arrival in June and the time of your departure, the retreat of yourself and Mr. Zemaj and others in September, that was the only incident that occurred where weapons were used and shots fired by KLA soldiers against FARK soldiers. There was no other incident involving a shooting by KLA soldiers against FARK soldiers during the period that you were in Kosovo in 1998, was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not the only incident. There was also the incident of the 10th of July in Prapaqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, you've described the 10th of July incident when shots were fired in the air. Leave that aside for a moment. There was never any other incident in which shots were fired at FARK officers, was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we leave aside the 10th of July incident, then okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to be absolutely clear about this. When you say "okay," you agree with the suggestion that I'm making to you. There is no other incident in which KLA soldiers or anybody with the KLA shot FARK soldiers during that period of time, was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said "okay"; that means yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, very specifically, I want to put two suggestions to you. There was never, in 1998, any incident in which --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'll just wait for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I just want to be very specific with you. There was never during 1998 any incident in which Ramush Haradinaj shot and killed a FARK soldier in front of Tahir Zemaj's eyes, was there? That never happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is a bit unclear to me. You're saying there was not an incident with Ramush Haradinaj that he never shot somebody in the presence of Tahir Zemaj. I don't know. I was not present everywhere, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did Tahir Zemaj ever suggest to you that Ramush Haradinaj had in his presence shot and killed a FARK officer during 1998? Was that suggestion ever made to you by Tahir Zemaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This question is very clear. Now I can respond very directly. He never told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And you were never told of an incident when a group of FARK officers were machine-gunned by KLA soldiers in front of another group of FARK officers, killing a group of FARK soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not clear about this question. I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Nobody ever reported to you during 1998 an incident in which a group of FARK soldiers, in the presence of other FARK soldiers, were machine-gunned and killed by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had information that they were wounded, they were ill-treated, and they were beaten, but not that they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That is a reference to the 4th of July incident; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like now, if I may, just to turn to some questions about the Prapaqan barracks. Now, you say, in your 92 ter statement, that you and the officers and soldiers with whom you had entered Kosovo moved into the Prapaqan barracks on the 10th of July. This is paragraph 41. Is that date correct, the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you please be provided with a copy of the blue cross-examination file. And you're now going to be given a blue file which contains a number of documents, some of which are documents that you have produced and some of which are documents that have been provided by other people. And I'd like you, please, to ask you, first of all, to turn to tab 5, which, for the record, is Exhibit P188. Now, first of all, can I ask you: Have you ever seen that document before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, do you agree that it indicates that the barracks at Prapaqan had been opened as a KLA military facility on the 8th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw this document before. I was not aware of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But it is correct, isn't it, that when you moved into the Prapaqan barracks, you were moving into a facility that had been set up and opened by the existing KLA officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was not aware of such planning. I personally was not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn to tab 6, please. That seems to be, just again, for the record, tab 6 is Exhibit D39. This document shows a list of KLA soldiers who were allocated to the Prapaqan barracks, 64 of them in all, on the 8th of July. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, it's right, isn't it, that when you moved into the Prapaqan barracks, there was a group of existing KLA volunteers who joined the soldiers that you had brought with you inside the Prapaqan barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were some soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They were locals, they were Gjakovars; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't know what area they came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Obviously, we can see from the document that they're all recorded as coming from Gjakove, do you see that, apart from the last two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the document, but the question was whether they were Gjakovars, and I'm speaking about the time when I went to the barracks, or the school barracks as they were called at that time. I can't respond to you in any other way. I didn't know at the time what area they came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's a perfectly fair comment. Witness 17, I'm going to suggest to you that in the first couple of days, after you started to move in, there was a certain degree of friction between the existing KLA volunteers who were there and the officers and soldiers that you brought with you. Now, do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, just the incident of the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'm going to suggest to you that that's what underlay the incident of the 10th of July. You and the officers who you'd brought with you, I suggest, took the view that the 64 volunteers who were allocated to the barracks were not proper soldiers. Do you remember forming that view?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is a provoking question. I did not say that they were not true or proper soldiers. The question was whether they were Gjakovars, and I said I didn't know where they came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 17, I think you misunderstood Mr. Emmerson. The question of whether you knew or whether you did not know at the time whether these soldiers were from Gjakove is -- we left that issue. This was the next question. Mr. Emmerson suggested to you that there was tension and that you considered them, wherever they came from, not to be proper soldiers. Did you develop that opinion at the time? That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not have any opinion on them until the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, I want to suggest that the confrontation that took place on the 10th of July arose not over some trivial dispute about a salute but over the fact that the KLA volunteers, who were barracked along with your soldiers and officers at the Prapaqan barracks, were treated by your colleagues as second-class soldiers, and that that is what Ramush Haradinaj had come to remonstrate about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because you weren't present during the first part of the conversation when he arrived, were you? You told us in your statement, I think, elsewhere engaged in training at the time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever discover that that was, in fact, the origin of the dispute on the 10th, that in effect Mr. Haradinaj was saying, "I gave you these barracks, I put my own volunteers in the barracks, and now they're being ill-treated by the soldiers who've come in"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that our presence at the Prapaqan barracks was something that was agreed upon by Tahir Zemaj and Ramush. As about these small arguments before the 10th of July, I'm not aware of those because I was involved in the training of soldiers during the whole time. I was preparing the artillery group, as I was an expert in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You have also described two meetings that immediately followed that, on the 10th and 11th of July, when the differences were hammered out and resolved between Mr. Zemaj and Mr. Haradinaj in private on the 10th and then formalised on the 11th. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were meetings and conversations.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And they resulted in the formation of three brigades and the distribution of the FARK officers across those three brigades, did they not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The formation of the three brigades was before we entered Kosova. The brigades had already been formed, but Tahir agreed with Ramush on the location, whether it was okay for these brigades to go to the right place at the right time, and then on their structure. I know that Tahir had conversations with Ramush about this, but I'm not sure about the way they discussed the organisation because I was not present in those talks. I know that Ramush and Tahir came out of that room where they had the talks, and they discussed among themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You described these brigades that were formed and distributed or distributed -- sorry. Let me start the question again. You described the brigades that were then located in Baran and Prapaqan and so forth as FARK brigades, but in reality they were intended to be and were mixed brigades, were they not, which consisted of some of the soldiers you'd brought in and some of the volunteers who were already within Kosovo under the banner of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had three brigades that had been formed in Papaj in northern Albania, and they were 131, 133, and 134. The 134th Brigade was complete. It had its military staff and soldier structure, while the 131st and 133rd only had a superior officer structure. In the military sense, the mobilisation was conducted in Kosovo according to the agreement. We never took soldiers from the KLA staffs or from a territorial staff without the permission of the territorial staff. I did this in my brigade especially. Later, there was a discussion about numbers, whether they would be called 131st or number 1 or 133rd. I think that Ramush and Tahir discussed the numbers of the brigades, which was not important at all, what number would be given to the brigades I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I entirely understand that's not important. But in terms of the numbers of soldiers in the brigades, that may be a little more important. Your notes indicate that you had 200-odd soldiers under your command in the 3rd Brigade, is that right, or were there more than that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the beginning, yes. Later, all the territorial staffs were subordinated to us in the area where I operated, and the number became much larger.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. So 200 to start with. You -- can you give us some idea of the number that were left at Prapaqan under the 1st Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not responsible for the -- I'm speaking about 131st -- 134th, which was given the number the 1st Brigade. I don't know how many soldiers were left behind in Prapaqan. Tahir Zemaj was responsible for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not asking --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was formed in Tropoje already.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not asking for a specific number but an approximation. Were there more than a hundred soldiers left at Prapaqan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Albania, we entered in Kosovo with over a hundred soldiers from the 134th Brigade, and then mobilisation occurred in Kosovo and the number became larger. I don't know exactly how many soldiers there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So all of the soldiers that you brought with you stayed with Tahir Zemaj in Prapaqan, did they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were in his brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then they were joined by what you call local mobilisation; in other words, local KLA volunteers, is that right, who joined them under Tahir Zemaj's command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that, with our arrival in Kosovo, mobilisation occurred and the soldiers were taken from the territorial local staffs in the villages, and that's how they joined in.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the 200 people who were under your command at Baran then, these were not FARK soldiers who had come in with you but people who were either existing members of the Territorial Defence or existing KLA volunteers. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we went to Baran on the 12th of July, and upon the formation of the brigade, there was an agreement that the mobilisation would be done by the territorial staffs of the villages, with the permission of the commanders or the staffs who would send them to the brigade in order for the numbers to increase. Of course, until we went there, there were KLA staffs that were operating and also territorial, local staffs that then were subordinated to the brigade. I'm speaking about Lugu i Baranit area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. That's very helpful, and if I can just clarify it with a yes or no question. It follows from what you've told us that the soldiers under your command were not soldiers that you brought with you into Kosovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Now, could we look, please, behind tab 8 of the blue file, and I just want to get the picture clear as to the process of amalgamation that was taking place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you also seek some clarification. I don't know whether I understood the witness well. In paragraph 47 of the 92 ter statement, the witness is referring to the 1st Brigade as the former 134th; the 2nd Brigade as the former 133rd; and the 3rd Brigade, again, the former 134th; whereas, in his testimony today, he's talking about 131, 133, and 134, whereas, I see that there's a difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's unclear to me. You might be better -- in a better position to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, yes, I can if that would assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 17, just to be clear, your 92 ter statement, at paragraph 47, describes these brigades in relation to the numbers, and it says -- I'll just read it to you, rather than ask you to look it up. It says: "The 1st Brigade was based in Prapaqan, formerly the 134th ..." Now, just taking that. Was the 1st Brigade in Prapaqan, did it consist of soldiers who had formerly been in the 134th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade did not change. We always called it the 134th Brigade, so these were soldiers from 134th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You then say: "The 2nd Brigade based in Irzniq was the formerly the 133 Brigade." Now, let me be clear, were there any soldiers as such in the 133 Brigade when you entered Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you that only the 134 Brigade was formed completely with soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So when you say the 2nd Brigade in Irzniq was formerly the 133 Brigade, there was no 133 Brigade, was there, not in reality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This brigade was formed later on in Kosova when the mobilisation of soldiers took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We'll come to that in a moment, but you say in your statement that the 2nd Brigade was made up of what was formerly the 133 Brigade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness answered this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour's happy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It may exist on paper, but it was formed, as he said, later.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then you say that the 3rd Brigade, based in the Baran Valley, was formerly the 134th Brigade. That's what your statement says. Now, is that what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It should be 131. I think it is a typo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. But again - and the same answer presumably follows - there were no soldiers until the 131 Brigade. It existed only in paper when you entered Kosovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a military staff that was ready to enter Kosova, and it was already planned for the mobilisation to take place in Kosova, because it was impossible to enter Kosova with three brigades at the same time with more than 100 soldiers to cross the Albanian-Kosovar border without being uncovered by the enemy. This was the basic idea, to form one brigade fully, and the other two, to form them later on in Kosova, to fill in the numbers with soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we could just look, please, at tab 8. This is a document -- I'm sorry. For the record, tab 8 is Exhibit P192. This is a document signed by Tahir Zemaj which is expressed as a request for the appointment and job specification of military officers pursuant to the 10th of July agreement. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it's addressed to the Dukagjini Plain Operative Staff. I just want to understand this, first of all, the nature of the document, because you I think produced one version of this document. At this point Mr. Zemaj is making a request to Mr. Haradinaj; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct as for what is written on the paper and the signature of this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- meaning the signature, not just what it writes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And of the 20 named officers, five of them were existing officers of the Dukagjini KLA, were they not? And I'm referring to number 8, Shemsedin Cekaj; number 13, Driton Zeneli; number 18, Rrustem Tetaj; number 19, Skender Rexhahmetaj; and number 20, Gani Gjukaj, so 8, 13, 18, 19, and 20. Five of those officers were KLA officers in the Dukagjini area, were they not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't take note of all the numbers. You said 8, 9, 19, and 20? Maybe I missed just one number. Maybe you said 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me go through them with you then individually. Number 8, Shemsedin Cekaj, he was not somebody who came with you. He was an existing KLA commander, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We found him in Kosova; that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The same is true of number 13, Driton Zeneli?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Number 18, Rrustem Tetaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was the fifth.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Number 19, Skender Rexhahmetaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And number 20, Gani Gjukaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now could you look to tab 9, please, which is Exhibit P193. This document sets out another request and proposal from Mr. Zemaj to the Dukagjini Plain Operative Staff for the way in which officers were to be distributed, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can see from the document, I agree with you, but I'm not sure about the signature because this signature is not Tahir Zemaj's signature. And this goes for the first document as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you this, please: You say in your witness statement - and I'm looking at paragraph 53 at the document - you say: "The 2nd or 133 Brigade was located in Bardhaniq village, Decan municipality. This brigade was not properly staffed and, therefore, never properly came into existence. The commander of the brigade, Kemal Shaqiri, later left to take up duty in the Drenica HQ." Now, I just want to be clear about this, Witness 17, because on this document, the commander of the 2nd Brigade is listed as Shemsedin Cekaj, and Kemal Shaqiri is listed as the Chief of Staff of the 1st Brigade. Can you help us about that, please? Was the commander of the 2nd Brigade Shemsedin Cekaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning, as for Kemal Shaqiri, he was planned to be the commander of the 133 Brigade upon our arrival in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: My question is: When the three brigades were set up after the 10th of July agreement, is it correct that Shemsedin Cekaj, who's testified in this court about his position in this regard, is it correct that he was, in fact, appointed to be the commander of the 2nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, when Kemal Shaqiri left for Drenica for the needs of the army there, and after Tahir Zemaj authorised his leaving, the brigade was led by Musa Gjakova. Shemsedin Cekaj was part of that structure, but personally I have no knowledge that he was commander of that brigade. Musa Gjakova was a person who was leading the brigade at that time. This is what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And where this document refers to Kemal Shaqiri as being the Chief of Staff of the 1st Brigade, what is your response to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't show results in the duty of commander of the 2nd Brigade. He stayed for some time in the 134 Brigade, Kemal Shaqiri, as a Chief of Staff of this brigade, but for a very brief period because he left for Drenice.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. If we look now, please, behind tab 10, this is annex 10 to your witness statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Did you wish to say something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just wanted to explain something about the names that you mentioned, the 20 officers and those five who were already in Kosova before we entered it. I just wanted to point out that, on the 2nd of July, there was a meeting held. All these senior officers attended this meeting which was held in Isniq, and the remaining officers joined the brigades with the exception of Rrustem Tetaj. I think it would be of use to know this fact because this is what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we look behind tab 10 in the bundle, this is annex 10 to your statement. We see a document signed by Ramush Haradinaj ordering the formation of the 3rd Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to this document, it is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could look behind tab 11 for a moment, Witness 17. I'm not going to take you to these documents individually, but these are each of them authorisations and orders signed by Ramush Haradinaj for the establishment of each of the three brigades. I suggest. Can you please look through them and confirm that. And, for the record, this is Exhibit P199, P194, P200, P198, P201 - sorry - and P197. Do you see those documents, Witness 17?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the first document under tab 11, dated 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you to go through them individually, Witness 17, but they are each of them authorisations and orders similar to the one that you have produced for the formation of the three brigades, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are instructions or authorisations which indicate the formation of the three brigades which were already formed, as I said. Only the name of the brigade -- brigades changes. The numbers changes -- change, but there are no changes in the military structure and in the structure of senior officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You earlier referred to annex 10 to the 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that, provisionally, P numbers have been assigned to those documents. That would be----

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It would be P890.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- P890. For the record, it's easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I want you to help, if you can, us understand that then, from that point onwards, from the 12th of July onwards, when these authorisations were signed and the brigades began to distribute themselves and set up, what was your understanding of the command relationship between Tahir Zemaj and Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The relationship between Tahir Zemaj and Ramush Haradinaj had a tendency to become closer.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not asking you about their personal relationship, although that answer's helpful. I'm asking about their command relationship. You see, on the face of these documents, we have Tahir Zemaj making a request and then a response from Ramush Haradinaj in the form of an authorisation. And I just want to understand whether, going forwards from the 12th of July, it was accepted that Tahir Zemaj was subordinate to Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said earlier that I looked at these document, but the first document and the second one, namely, the request by Tahir Zemaj, the signature does not correspond to his. I'm sure that this is not his signature. I know for a fact that there were discussions amongst them. There were tendencies to join forces. This I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Forget the individual documents. Concentrate on annex 10, the document you've produced, which is an order for the formation of the brigade over which you were the commander, which is signed by Mr. Haradinaj. What I want to understand from you, not on the documents themselves, but from your understanding of the command relationship at the time, is simply this: Who was in command of whom? Was Ramush Haradinaj subordinate to Tahir Zemaj in your view; Tahir Zemaj subordinate to Ramush Haradinaj; or were they operating, so to speak, on a parallel? What was your understanding of their command relationship?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask counsel on this one question to be more specific as to time. It's phrased from the 12th of July --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On the 12th of July then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you help us at all, please, Witness 17? What was in command of who, or did you not know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of operative units was Tahir Zemaj, commander of the three brigades that entered Kosova; while the commander of the Dukagjini Plain and of the units of the KLA, after we entered Kosova, we realised him to be Ramush Haradinaj. Up to the 21st of August, this is how it functioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no subordinates, or nobody was commander of somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So you say, up until the 21st of August when Tahir Zemaj became overall commander, he was on an equal and independent standing, in your view, to Ramush Haradinaj; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that he commanded with the operative units of the three brigades that entered Kosova, while Ramush continued to perform his duty as commander of the Dukagjini Plain in the function that we found him. And the meetings show that the aim was to reach an agreement between the two sides, an agreement that we entered in Oslo. We tried in all possible ways to implement the Oslo agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. In your 92 ter statement, at paragraph 59, there is a sentence which reads: "All local staff in my area of responsibility were automatically supposed to be called FARK soldiers." "All local staff in my area of responsibility were automatically supposed to be called FARK soldiers." Now, I want to ask you: Is that what you meant to say, that the people who were under your command in Baran were expected to refer to themselves as FARK soldiers rather than KLA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask my colleague to, when he presents this question to the witness, to read the last clause of that sentence. I believe it is important for the -- for the understanding of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. I'm not going to do that, with respect, because I'm not asking about any individual or any loyalties. I'm simply asking about whether it's correct that officers under this witness's command were expected to refer to themselves as FARK soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question can be put in re-examination if you would like to create a better context, Mr. Kearney. You're allowed to do so of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, could you answer the question, Witness 17. Is it your evidence that the officers and soldiers under your - let's just take the soldiers - that the soldiers under your command were expected to refer to themselves as FARK soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that they should refer to themselves as such. We had already formed our brigades in Tropoje in northern Albania. This is how we entered Kosova. We were subordinated to a command, the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Kosova. We had our designated tasks and duties, and we acted pursuant to these orders. The units that we found in Kosova, as well as the commanders we found there, we did our best to cooperate with them and to reach an agreement on future activities. When I arrived at Baran on 12th of July, the mobilisation of soldiers was agreed upon, the area of responsibility of the brigade was designated, and my area of responsibility included Raushiq, Loxh, Baran i Eperm, Baran i Ulet, Kotradic, Vranoc, and up to Kepuz. All these villages were all under my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you. I was not asking about the villages under your command. I think you've answered the question which I was asking which is: You did not expect FARK soldiers, or soldiers under your command, to refer to themselves as FARK soldiers. You would expect them to refer to KLA soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't understand your question now. It's really mixed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, very well. Let me put it to you clearly. Your witness statement says that soldiers under your command were automatically supposed to be called FARK soldiers. I have asked you whether that was intended to suggest that they were supposed to refer to themselves, that is, to present themselves to other people, as members of the FARK, or whether you would expect them to refer to themselves as members of the KLA. I'm trying to understand whether you're suggesting that there was a separate designation of FARK soldiers. Now do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A separate designation was the designation of my area of responsibility. All those villages that fell in my area of responsibility were under the command of my brigade. So no soldier was allowed to declare himself a member of this or that unit, especially not to the villagers, because soldiers should report to their respective commanders and not to civilians or ordinary villagers. In my opinion, there is no need for a soldier to report to a civilian and tell him to which organisation he belongs.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I'm going to look now, please, behind tab 1, which is your notes of the various events that occurred over this period; and, in particular, I want to look at the passage of your notes - this is tab 1, Witness 17 - the passage of your notes that deals with the meetings that you had on the 13th of July. If you could find that for us in the manuscript part of your notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For those following in English, it is page 14 of the English translation. Tab 1 is annex 1 to the witness's 92 ter statement with proposed Exhibit Number P886.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I'm told that - if you just bear with me for a moment - if you look as the numbers that are stamped on this document, you will find -- which is stamped in the top right-hand corner in the Albanian, you will find the passage that I'm asking you to look at on, at U008-5677 at line 13 or thereabouts. Now, have you found the page, Witness 17?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher might help, 5677, on the left-hand side of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, first of all, Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, before we continue there, you were referring to the English page 14?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But may I draw your attention, and also Mr. Kearney's attention, to something I noticed; that is, the witness yesterday, when he testified about the ten names of people that would be wanted or missing, he said: "I jotted that down the day after I heard about it," or when he exactly received that is unclear. I noted that on page 13 - and it has some effect also on page 14 - that above the military police, in the original, you find a new date, that is, the 13th of July, 1998; whereas, as it appears now, it looks as only on page 14 we're moving to the 13th of July; whereas, in fact, in the original, it does already halfway page 13. Mr. Kearney, it seems to be a translation or a transcript error. I don't know whether you noticed it. My attention was drawn to it because on the basis of the document itself, I had some difficulties to understand that it was jotted down not on the 12th but not 13th; whereas, it appears, at least in English, already to be written down on the 12th. But comparison with the original made clear to me that actually it is something that is under the heading of the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And I believe that was what the witness testified to yesterday, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's, of course, what he testified to, but which I had some difficulties in reconciling with what I found in the document until I consulted the original. I don't know whether page 13 could be replaced by a better copy, including the date above the line where it reads "military police."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Perhaps, at the break, I can check with our interpreters, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's not a lot of interpretation to be done. It's just looking at 130798.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you've found the passage that I've asked you to look at, have you, Witness 17? Have you found the passage that I've asked you to look at on page 5677?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have here on the screen a page with a different date. If we are talking about the list of --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, we're not --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- people sought, that's another page.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Forget about that, Witness 17. I was just making a comment on something you told us yesterday. It's not related to the question Mr. Emmerson will ask you, from what I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm asking you about page 5677. Now, first of all, Witness 17, can you please confirm that, immediately after your arrival in Baran, you travelled around the villages trying to recruit people to join the 3rd Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went immediately to the villages, and I informed the commands of the villages in the region.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I want to ask you about the meeting that you held with the inhabitants of Buqan at 6.00 in the evening, that is, 1800 hours, on the 13th of July because you gave them a briefing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And from the notes that we have, it appears that you told them about the formation of the 3rd Brigade and you told them of the mobilisation of soldiers aged 18 to 35 in operational units and in Territorial Defence units from 18 to 65. Is that what you told them when you arrived in Buqan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then it appears from your notes that you said this to them: "The question whether there is a KLA or a government army has no sense because the leadership has agreed upon that KLA is the core or the foundation of a Kosovo modern army; therefore, we are the KLA and the KLA are us. Consequently, all the dilemmas, whether the actions are coordinated or not, should be discarded." Is that the message that you were giving out to the village defence staffs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was my message because I was sure and clear pursuant to the Oslo agreement there -- that there were no dilemmas about the further structure and organisation. Everything was clear to me. That's why I said those words to the regional staffs wherever I went, and this was also our approach in the terrain, on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, may I also draw your attention to page 7611 yesterday, where the witness testified about from whatever routes the forces would come, they would call it by the name best known to the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Names are not, perhaps not always, reflecting, at least, that's suggested in the answer of the witness yesterday, that this was very convenient to approach the matter in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, at the same time, he's saying an armed force of which the bulk came from this --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of course, that isn't in his testimony. The testimony is that the soldiers under his command were all locally recruited people who were formerly village defence staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of a force, the bulk of which -- now he's talking about the overall, of which would come from the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I interrupted too quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't suggest that the bulk came from the FARK.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I previously consulted with my colleagues, and I'm wondering whether it's going into further detail here --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- would assist with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I've finished with that topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The last topic I want to take you to before taking a break would be to ask you help us at page 5731 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Help the witness to page 5731 in the same document; and for those following in English, it's page 81 in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Witness 17, is this a list of the commanders of the 3rd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A list of the commanders of 131st Brigade, later called the 3rd Brigade, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to ask you about a couple of people first of all on that list. The first five names on that list appear on the order establishing the 3rd Brigade that we have looked at. Can I ask you about Musa Dragaj very briefly. He seems to have been given the title the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 3rd Brigade. Is that right, is that his title?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later, because the change in senior officers was done according to the needs on the ground, and that's why the name of a person appears sometimes in one brigade and sometimes in another brigade. This was in the beginning. Rrustem Berisha was the commander of the 131st Brigade. But because of the developments after we entered Kosova, he had to remain in Junik, and I acted as commander of that brigade further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that. And Musa Dragaj was one of your immediate subordinates; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was planned to be in the beginning, but he never came to my brigade in Baran.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I'm not perfectly certain that the witness did understand your previous question where in his answer he was referring only to 3rd Brigade -- people in brigades; whereas, you asked about battalion, 3rd Battalion --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I did because of the documents we've seen, but I think the witness's last answer seems to supersede that and for the purposes of the questioning I'm putting to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to be clear, because I want to be absolutely certain of what you're saying, Witness 17. Is it your testimony - because you appreciate you're not the only witness to give evidence about who was at Baran - is it your testimony that Musa Dragaj was not serving at the school barracks in Baran under your command? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only for -- sorry, sorry. I confused Musa Dragaj with Musa Gjakova. There has been a change. Musa Dragaj was in Baran, yes, that's sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come back --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We'll come back to him. Just a couple further questions, if I may, still within the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you finish within two, three minutes, otherwise we'll have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sadri Selca, he was appointed by you as head of intelligence and counter-intelligence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not call it intelligence or counter-intelligence. We called it a person responsible for security in the brigade. Because after I arrived in Baran, I organised the sectors: The information sector, the logistics sector, the observation and cartography sector, and the security sector. In the beginning, the military police was formed on the 12th of July in Vranoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'll come back to the military police after the break. Finally this on this page before we break. I want to ask you about a man who is not on the list but who you refer to in your statement, at paragraph 77, as one of your officers, a man called Cufe Krasniqi. Can I ask you, please, what his command level was under your command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was commander of a platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a convenient moment. We'll have a break until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, before you continue, I was informed that there's a request from the Brahimaj Defence to have an opportunity to inspect the original of the notes of this Witness 17. Mr. Harvey, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first try to find out what the witness thinks about it. Witness 17, Defence counsel would like to have access to the original of your notes. Are you willing to make these notes available for, I take it, for inspection?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So not to be taken away forever. I don't know whether you would like to have an expert look at it or start just by yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Just start by myself, Your Honour, and we'll see where it goes from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any idea of how much time you'd think you'd need?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Only a matter of ten minutes or so, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 17, would you mind to give the original of your notes during the next break - I would then suggest, Mr. Harvey - to Mr. Harvey so that he can have a look at the original?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't mind, but not for him to check it for a long time, one day, two days. I would like it for me -- to be returned to me immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It won't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be returned and Mr. Harvey, it's one of his professional duties not to change, not to -- well, just look at it, inspect it. And if he would need it, well, let's say, for expert opinion, then he would return it to you, then ask for such -- for an opportunity to have an expert look at it as well - I don't know whether this will happen or not - and then he might address the Chamber and ask the Chamber to invite you to make it available for expert -- for expertise as well. But then let's not anticipate on that. The only thing, at this moment, Mr. Harvey's asking is to get it for ten minutes and it then to be returned to you. But whatever will happen, the Chamber would already like to instruct you to keep your notes; that is, not to lose them, burn them, sell them, whatever, so that you keep the original version of the notes which have been copied, but only the copied version available at this moment to us. So then you're invited to give the original, at the end of this session, for inspection to Mr. Harvey. Thank you for your cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 17, looking back, please, then at that list of commanders of the 3rd Brigade, I want to ask you now about Din Krasniqi. Now, you say, in your statement, Din Krasniqi was the Baran Valley commander. Can you just, please, explain to us within this list of the command of the 3rd Brigade what his formal role was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krasniqi was some kind of coordinate after the brigade came to Baran, after the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've included him on this page where you list the brigade commanders. We can see that he's a paediatrician. What is the significance of him being one of the people listed amongst the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not. There was an office, a health office in the brigade, and he checked the soldiers. That's why he is in this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was he a medical officer of the brigade then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He checked the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. I think you accept, don't you, that he was formally under your command? That's to be found in your witness statement at paragraph 56.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon the arrival of the brigade and my arrival in Baran, automatically, he had to become my subordinate; but, in fact, we worked in a parallel fashion, as far as he was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll come to that in a moment, if I may. Now, you say various things in your witness statement about his role, and I just want to explore some of them with you. You say that, when you first arrived, he introduced himself as Baran Valley commander and told you that he had been appointed to that position by Ramush Haradinaj, paragraph 55. I just want to be clear about this. First of all, do you have any personal knowledge about the manner in which Din Krasniqi came to be appointed or chosen as the Baran Valley commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We've heard evidence from Cufe Krasniqi that the villages of the Baran Valley organised themselves and that it was he, Cufe, who had nominated Din Krasniqi for selection as the Baran Valley commander. That's transcript 5471, lines 2 to 5. Can I be clear about this, as far as you are aware, was the Baran Valley command already organised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the villagers were organised already before we went there, this is something that was clear to us; but the fact that Cufe appointed Din as commander, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Put shortly, just so that the Trial Chamber understands, you have no real knowledge of how the Baran Valley had organised its command before you arrived; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that I am not aware that Cufe appointed Din Krasniqi as commander of the villages of Lugu i Baranit, but I was aware that a part of the villages were organised already.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, at paragraph 59 of your statement, you suggest that Din Krasniqi was having regular meetings with Ramush Haradinaj during the time that you were in Baran from the 12th of July onwards. I just want to ask you, please: What is the basis for your suggestion that they were having regular meetings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact is that he had meetings with the village commanders once a week, although it was not necessary, because I was there and I had daily meetings, briefings at 7.00 every evening and he then, of course, reported further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just pause for a moment. You didn't know at the time, did you, that there were any meetings between Ramush Haradinaj and the village commanders going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Lugu i Baranit, I know that Din met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, your reference to 5471 [sic] seems not to be very solid; at least, I find something totally different there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Then I'll check my reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just so that we're clear, in paragraph 59 of your witness statement, you are shown the minutes of a meeting attended by Ramush Haradinaj with Baran Valley staff commanders on the 29th of July, and you say, and I quote: "I did not know that Ramush Haradinaj was having such meetings with KLA village commanders." That's what your witness statement says. Now, I just want clear, at the time from the 12th of July onwards, why is it that you say that meetings were taking place between Ramush Haradinaj and Din Krasniqi. On what basis do you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of what I already said, that every week he called the village commanders and had meetings with them, but he never reported to me on what was discussed at these meetings with them, and I believe that he continued his further contacts with Ramush.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm not concerned about general belief. I'm pressing you for specifics here, Witness 17, about meetings between Ramush Haradinaj and Din Krasniqi. First of all, did Din Krasniqi himself tell you that he'd had meetings with Ramush Haradinaj? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Din Krasniqi said that he had been appointed by Ramush. He told me that on the 12th of July when I arrived in Vranoc, when we had the meeting with the commanders of the villages and with Krasniqi. And, according to the way he behaved, he never was willing to leave that post. He continued to be in that post even further; although, he knew that, after the 12th of July, it was the responsibility of the brigade, and everything had to be done in the framework of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to be clear, please. I understand what you're saying about the position before your arrival. I want to know whether you have any basis for suggesting, after the time that you arrived, that there were meetings, regular meetings, going on between Din Krasniqi and Ramush Haradinaj. Now, if the position is that you don't know that there were meetings going on, then please tell us; if the position is that you do know, then please tell us how you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to object at this stage. This question has been asked and answered --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Not --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- at this stage. He said that, based on the way that Din Krasniqi behaved in his unwillingness to leave his former position, that's the conclusion he drew. It is my belief that is testimony --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If that's the extent in the evidence, then, in our submission, it remains an unsupported assertion. I'm giving the witness the opportunity to tell us what the basis for his assertion is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll allow the question to be put, and I invite the witness to answer the question. Perhaps you put it again to him, Mr. Emmerson, because he might be misled. Meanwhile, I resolve the matter of "5471" should be "5741."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 17, the question I am asking you is: Do you know for a fact that there were meetings taking place between the two of them, that is, Ramush Haradinaj and Din Krasniqi, after the 12th of July when you became commander; and if so, please tell us how you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not attend these meetings because geographically it was part of the territory where I could not move about at all times and see who is meeting whom. He was responsible for health issues in the brigade, and I know that he had meetings with the village commanders and that he reported further to Ramush. I know this, because some village commanders who did not go to those meetings told me about these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the commanders of the villages told you that Din Krasniqi regularly visited them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the meeting with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And are you saying that one or more of the village commanders told you that Din Krasniqi had had meetings regularly with Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Din Krasniqi with Ramush.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Are you saying somebody told --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to get more direct. You explained to us that you were not present when Din Krasniqi met with Ramush Haradinaj. It was in the area you had no access to. How did you know that these regular meetings took place? Who told you? What did you observe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, from the meetings that Din Krasniqi held with the village commanders, and my information came from certain of those persons who told me that Din further reports to Ramush.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, who told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a name. I don't know exactly the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And are you able to tell us whether the information was reliable or not, if you don't know who it was who told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the further development of the events, I can say that this information was reliable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I'm also intrigued by it. You said you don't have a name. Do you remember what position? Was this a village commander of a certain village? Do you remember which village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I said that I don't have knowledge about the names; but as things developed later on, it turned out that the contacts between Din and Ramush were regular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's still a bit mysterious to me. Could you confirm that your source of knowledge was one of the village commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One or more? Did you hear it from one or from more village commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I cannot recall. Years have passed, nine years, and I'm not able to recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did they tell you that Din Krasniqi reported to Haradinaj, which not necessarily includes that they met? Could you tell us in more detail what this person told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot talk in more details. From what I recall, I was informed by that individual that Din reported further about his contacts with the village commanders, and it implies the situation in the zone and the activities of the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think you accept, don't you, that you have no idea, if such contacts did take place, what may or may not have been said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about the subject discussed during these contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you were referring to contacts. Were you referring to contacts between Ramush Haradinaj and Din Krasniqi? Because the last time the word "contact" was used, it was the contact between the village commanders and Din Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, yes, let me make it absolutely clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You have no idea, if there was any contact between Mr. Haradinaj and Mr. Krasniqi, you have no idea what passed between them, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that's a -- that question has two parts in it. One misstates this witness's earlier testimony --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me break the question down again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Assuming that there were contacts between Ramush Haradinaj and Din Krasniqi, do you accept, Witness 17, that you do not know what, if anything, was discussed between them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were contacts; but, as I said, I don't know the subject matter of those contacts. I don't know what they discussed between themselves. I think my answer is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, presumably, as brigade commander, you had the authority to issue instructions to Din Krasniqi; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on how he understood those instructions and how obedient he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not asking at the moment about whether he was always obedient, but you had the authority to issue instructions to him under the command structure that was in place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already said, it depends on the way he understood those instructions. It depends how -- on how the other side interpreted those instructions; and in this concrete case, Din Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You say in your witness statement, at paragraph, 59 that you were informed by two of your officers that a kind of anarchy existed within the command of Din Krasniqi, whereby orders were not being carried out and the chain of command was not respected. I want to ask you, please: What do you mean by "kind of anarchy"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I meant is that certain soldiers, who were under his command before the arrival of the brigade at Baran, continued their activities and continued to present -- to present obstacles in the further creation of the structure, military structure, in Baran.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
